own_solution.law: Transverse Doppler effect (time dilation of the source): f_abs = f0 sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2), so to leading order Delta f = f0 v^2/(2 c^2), with f0 = E/h and v = 2 pi r f_rot
assumptions: emission direction in the lab is perpendicular to the source velocity (absorber on the axis), so no first-order Doppler shift
absorber at rest in an inertial lab frame

defect_reasons.other: T1355 omits 'at the same rotation frequency', which TC381 states; the problem's stated 600 Hz makes the natural reading unchanged frequency, but the two R sentences differ in more than wording.

notes: With r = 15.7 cm: Delta f scales as r^2, (15.7/12)^2 = 1.71174, so Delta f = 6.785e6 Hz. The earlier-run sentences and the vacuum-pump pulley sentences are disconnected. Every number-bearing sentence states 3.7 cm. The 'a little larger' sentences carry no number.
